paramsNote: Engine parameters supplied by the coordinator. They do NOT necessarily equal the printed plan dimensions below - see overview for the values actually printed on the plan sheets.

widthAtBase.note: Base layout outside-to-outside (p8). Only the non-beveled method is drawn for this model.

baseSideLength.note: One base bay, measured on the base layout sheet (p8).

overview.doorOpeningNote: This plan set never states a finished door rough opening. The doorway is a framed gable dormer; the only related numbers are the double 2x6 / 38x140 header at 6'-3" / 1905 mm and the (2) trimmer studs at 6'-8" / 2032 mm (p14).
overview.buildMethod: Non-beveled method only. The Model Specific Notes sheet (p3) says: minimum 2x4 / 38x89 lumber, and 'This zome should be constructed in the non beveled method, as the frames are too deep to run through the table saw.' The bevel-angle column is still printed but is not used for this build method.
overview.geometryNote: Zome, 10-sided plan, 5 concentric bands of rhombic panels labelled z1 (top/centre) through z5 (widest), plus two special half panels. All struts are the same length; only the corner (miter) angles and the dihedral-derived bevel angles change band to band.

length.note: Overall panel length - identical for every regular panel edge and for the sloped edges of the special panels.

crossSection.note: The Model Specific Notes sheet calls for a minimum of 2x4 / 38x89 lumber. The materials list buys (115) 2x4x10 / 38x89x3m for the frame panels. Deeper members may be substituted if the plan is scaled.

strut.bevelNote: Bevel is not a single value. Each panel band has a top bevel (the two struts pointing toward the centre/top) and a bottom bevel (the two struts pointing outward/down). Where two bands meet the bevels match. Not used in the non-beveled method, which is the method specified for this model. See panels[].bevels.
strut.miterNote: All miter angles in the plans are stated as OFF 90 degrees - i.e. the number is what you set the miter saw to. Within one regular panel every strut shares the same miter angle.

midLength.note: Width across the panel at mid height, outside framing; use for jig layout.
Plans warn that z4 and z5 are wider than they are tall - this dimension is the wide axis.

panels.position: Band 5 - widest band, at/near the base

midLength.note: Wide axis; z5 is wider than tall.

panels.planLabel: z4 half (base) - listed as 'z4 half horiz' in the component list
panels.type: special / triangle (base half of a z4, cut on the wide diagonal)
panels.position: Base course - sits on the base sections

edges.name: Two equal sloped sides
edges.note: PRINTED VALUE, BELIEVED WRONG. The triangle's own base and miters require 4' 8" / 1423 mm (the strut length). 5'-6 3/8" / 1686 mm is exactly the 30' / 9m zome strut length. See pdfIssues.

panels.planLabel: z5 half - listed as 'z5.5' in the component list
panels.type: special / triangle (vertical half of a z5)

geometryChecks.method: For a rhombus of side s with printed mid-width (short diagonal) d, the spanned corner angle is 2*asin((d/2)/s); the saw miter (off 90 deg) must equal |90 - that angle| or |90 - (180 - that angle)|. Computed from the imperial figures with s = 56 in.

specialPanels.check: Miters 33.1 / 23.8 / 33.1 give interior angles 56.9 / 66.2 / 56.9 (sum 180). Third side computed 1554 mm - matches the printed 5'-1 3/16" / 1554 mm.
Miters 15.6 / 52.8 / 52.8 give interior angles 105.6 / 37.2 / 37.2 (sum 180). With base 7'-5 1/4" / 2267 mm the equal sides must be 4' 8" / 1423 mm, not the printed 5'-6 3/8" / 1686 mm.

geometryChecks.metricCrossCheck: Every metric mid-length and side length re-checks to within 1 mm of the imperial value, and the metric miter computation reproduces the same results.
geometryChecks.conclusion: All five rhombus bands are internally consistent. The only dimensional error found is the z4 half (base) side length.

pdfIssues.issue: The z4 half (base) triangle has its two equal sloped sides dimensioned 5'-6 3/8" / 1686 mm. That is impossible for this panel: with the printed base of 7'-5 1/4" / 2267 mm and the printed miters (15.6 apex, 52.8 base), the equal sides must be 4' 8" / 1423 mm - the strut length, exactly as on the 20' and 30' sheets. 5'-6 3/8" / 1686 mm is precisely the 30' / 9m zome's strut length, so this is a copy-paste from the 30' plan set.
pdfIssues.severity: major - would produce 8 unusable base panels if cut as printed

pdfIssues.issue: The entire deck cut list is still in imperial (7'-6 1/2", 11'-10 5/16", 12'- 7/8", 6'- 1/4", 4'-8 5/8", 3'-5 1/16", 2'-1 7/16", 9 13/16") and the note reads 'Blocking Joists are 2' on center'. The deck drawing on the next sheet IS metric, so the two sheets disagree in units.
pdfIssues.severity: moderate - metric-only builders have no converted deck cut list

pdfIssues.sheet: Doorway Roof Panel C (p17), METRIC edition
pdfIssues.issue: The Roof Panel C cut list is still in imperial (1'-8 15/16", 3'-11 3/16", 3'-9 1/8", 4'-3 7/8") and the area is still '14 sq ft', even though the drawing beside it is fully metric.
pdfIssues.severity: moderate - metric-only builders have no converted values for this panel

pdfIssues.sheet: Doorway Roof Panel C (p17), imperial vs metric
pdfIssues.issue: The bottom edge of the roof sheathing is 1'-9 1/8" (537 mm) on the imperial sheet but 594 mm on the metric sheet. Rebuilding the quadrilateral from the other three printed edges (top 1232, height 1233, slant 1418) gives about 532 mm, so the imperial figure is the plausible one and 594 mm appears to be the error.

pdfIssues.sheet: Doorway Wall Panel D (p18), IMPERIAL edition
pdfIssues.issue: A stud is printed '7-5 1/8"' with no foot mark. The metric 2264 mm confirms it means 7'-5 1/8".

pdfIssues.sheet: Doorway Roof Panel C (p17), IMPERIAL edition
pdfIssues.issue: The sheathing height is printed '4- 9/16"' with no foot mark. The metric 1233 mm confirms it means 4'- 9/16".
The overall panel height (2376 mm) is dimensioned only on the metric sheet; the imperial sheet leaves that dimension off.
pdfIssues.severity: minor - missing dimension in one edition

pdfIssues.issue: The stud stock is described as '(2x6)' on the imperial sheet and '(38x89)' on the metric sheet. 2x6 is 38x140, so the two editions call for different material for the same part. The stud lengths themselves (2 1/8" / 54 and 1 1/4" / 32) do match.
No finished door rough-opening size is published anywhere. The only door numbers are the 6'-3" / 1905 mm double header and the 6'-8" / 2032 mm trimmer studs.

The component list calls for 8 base sections but the base layout is a 10-sided decagon. The two missing bays are taken up by the doorway assembly (the base-sections drawing labels the gap '(Door)'), but the plans never say this explicitly.

pdfIssues.sheet: Model Specific Notes (p3) / Regular Panel Dimensions (p6)
pdfIssues.issue: The bevel-angle rows are still printed in the panel table even though this model is explicitly to be built by the non-beveled method, and the drawing note says '(Bevel angle not used for non beveled method)'. Recorded here for completeness in case a builder scales down and uses the beveled method.
